# Song of Solomon Chapter 4 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**4:1** Behold [hinnakh], you [are] beautiful [yafah], my-darling [ra'yati]; behold [hinnakh], you [are] beautiful [yafah]. Your-eyes [einayikh] [are] doves [yonim] from-behind [mi-ba'ad] your-veil [le-tzammatekh]. Your-hair [sa'rekh] [is] like-a-flock [ke-eder] of-goats [ha-izzim] that-stream-down [she-galeshu] from-Mount [me-har] Gilead [Gil'ad].

**4:2** Your-teeth [shinnayikh] [are] like-a-flock [ke-eder] of-shorn-ewes [ha-qetzuvot] that-come-up [she-alu] from-the-washing [min ha-rachtzah], all-of-them [she-kullam] bearing-twins [mat'imot], and-none [ve-shakkula] among-them [ein bahem] is-bereaved.

**4:3** Like-a-thread [ke-chut] of-scarlet [ha-shani] [are] your-lips [siftotayikh], and-your-mouth [u-midbarekh] [is] lovely [naveh]. Like-a-slice [ke-felach] of-pomegranate [ha-rimmon] [is] your-temple [raqqatech] from-behind [mi-ba'ad] your-veil [le-tzammatech].

**4:4** Like-the-tower [ke-migdal] of-David [David] [is] your-neck [tzavvarekh], built [banuy] for-an-armory [le-talpiyyot]; a-thousand [elef] shields [ha-magen] are-hung [taluy] on-it [alav], all [kol] the-bucklers [shiltei] of-the-warriors [ha-gibborim].

**4:5** Your-two [shenei] breasts [shadayikh] [are] like-two [ki-shnei] fawns [oferim], twins [te'omei] of-a-gazelle [tzeviyah], that-graze [ha-ro'im] among the-lilies [ba-shoshannim].

**4:6** Until [ad] the-day [she-yafuach ha-yom] breathes and-the-shadows [ve-nasu ha-tzelalim] flee, I-will-go [elekh li] to the-mountain [el har] of-myrrh [ha-mor] and-to the-hill [ve-el giv'at] of-frankincense [ha-levonah].

**4:7** You [are] all [kullakh] beautiful [yafah], my-darling [ra'yati], and-there-is-no [u-mum] blemish [ein] in-you [bakh].

**4:8** With-me [itti] from-Lebanon [mi-Levanon], O-bride [kallah], with-me [itti] from-Lebanon [mi-Levanon] come [tavo'i]; descend [tashuri] from-the-top [me-rosh] of-Amana [Amanah], from-the-top [me-rosh] of-Senir [Senir] and-Hermon [ve-Chermon], from-the-dens [mi-me'onot] of-lions [arayot], from-the-mountains [me-harerei] of-leopards [nemerim].

**4:9** You-have-ravished [libbavtini] my-heart [libbavtini], my-sister [achoti], my-bride [kallah]; you-have-ravished [libbavtini] my-heart with-one [be-echad] of-your-eyes [me-einayikh], with-one [be-echad] chain [anaq] of-your-neck [mi-tzavveronayikh].

**4:10** How-beautiful [mah yofu] [are] your-loves [dodayikh], my-sister [achoti], my-bride [kallah]; how-much-better [mah tovu] [are] your-loves [dodayikh] than-wine [mi-yayin], and-the-fragrance [ve-re'ach] of-your-oils [shemanayikh] than-all [mi-kol] spices [besamim].

**4:11** Your-lips [siftotayikh] drip [tittofnah] nectar [nofet], O-bride [kallah]; honey [devash] and-milk [ve-chalav] [are] under your-tongue [tachat leshonekh], and-the-scent [ve-re'ach] of-your-garments [salmotayikh] [is] like-the-scent [ke-re'ach] of-Lebanon [Levanon].

**4:12** A-garden [gan] locked [na'ul] [is] my-sister [achoti], my-bride [kallah]; a-spring [gal] locked [na'ul], a-fountain [ma'yan] sealed [chatum].

**4:13** Your-shoots [shelachayikh] [are] an-orchard [pardes] of-pomegranates [rimmonim] with [im] choice [megadim] fruits [peri], henna [kefarim] with [im] nard [neradim],

**4:14** nard [nerd] and-saffron [ve-kharkom], calamus [qaneh] and-cinnamon [ve-qinnamon], with-all [im kol] trees [atzei] of-frankincense [levonah], myrrh [mor] and-aloes [va-ahalot], with-all [im kol] chief [rashei] spices [vesamim].

**4:15** A-fountain [ma'yan] of-gardens [gannim], a-well [be'er] of-living [chayyim] waters [mayim], and-streams [ve-nozlim] from-Lebanon [min Levanon].

**4:16** Awake [uri], O-north-wind [tzafon], and-come [u-vo'i], O-south-wind [teiman]; blow-upon [hafichi] my-garden [ganni], let-its-spices [yizzelu vesamav] flow. Let-my-beloved [yavo dodi] come [le-ganno] to-his-garden and-eat [ve-yokhal] its-choice [megadav] fruits [peri].

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — The wasf:** Verses 1-7 constitute a *wasf* (Arabic: "description"), a genre of praise poetry describing the beloved's body from head to toe (or vice versa). The imagery draws from pastoral and military spheres — goats, ewes, pomegranates, towers, shields.

**v.12 — "garden locked, fountain sealed":** The *gan na'ul* (locked garden) and *ma'yan chatum* (sealed fountain) are the Song's most discussed images. They represent the beloved's sexual exclusivity — she is a garden of delights that belongs to one person.

**v.13 — "orchard" (pardes):** A Persian loanword (from *paridaeza*, whence English "paradise"). Its presence is one indicator of the Song's late date.

*-- EMET*
